_schema: Open provenance/attribution issues found during translation, keyed by paper id. Each: slug, severity, summary, evidence, action_needed. These were surfaced by the translation agents and converted from internal halt-reports into tracked issues (Sept 2026). They are NOT resolved.

138.summary: A run of source scans filed with this paper belongs to a different paper, so one passage of the translation is missing.
evidence: Scan pages 7-15 (printed pp. 375-383) carry verso running-headers reading 'Werner Kornfeld' while the recto running-title reads 'Abhaengigkeit der metamorphotischen Kiemenrueckbildung usw.'

Their subject matter is transplantation and developmental mechanics (induction in transplants, synchrony/heterochrony, germ-cell determination, heteroplastic skin grafts), not tadpole gill resorption.
The string 'Kiemenrueckbildung' appears only in the running-title header, never in the body text of those pages.
The title page of the gill-resorption paper is absent from the scan set.
The translator declined to translate those pages rather than emit the wrong paper's text.
138.action_needed: Obtain the correct scans for the missing printed pages and translate them. Separately, settle the author's forename: the catalog says only 'Kornfeld', the translation's own byline reads 'Werner Kornfeld', and the halt-report treats the gill paper as by 'Walter Kornfeld'. The title page is needed to decide.

_153_koppanyi.summary: The pages carry Auguste Jellinek's study, not Koppanyi's own text; the running title is the series title. The catalogue already attributes the paper to Jellinek, so nothing is mis-stated publicly.
evidence: 'Die Replantation von Augen. VII.' is the collected-volume series title, not this paper's title.
The page-top author byline on every page reads 'Auguste Jellinek'.
Content: sighted, blind and transplanted-eye rats compared on a colour-discrimination learning task.
The translation faithfully renders what is actually on the pages (printed pp. 89-95).
_153_koppanyi.action_needed: None for attribution. Remaining: the translation file is still named after Koppanyi (internal only), and Jellinek's biography on the Authors page is a stub worth expanding now that her forename is confirmed.

55.summary: This paper had no modern-literature assessment of its own: the record filed under it described a different paper (the 1906 Egyptian praying-mantis study), so its dossier has been withdrawn rather than left showing the wrong science.
evidence: The Consensus questions stored for id55 asked about colour change and limb regeneration in praying mantises; the paper is about four malformed spiny dogfish from Trieste.
The stored methodology record read 'Established the Egyptian mantis as a tractable experimental insect' — that is id59's paper, and id59 carries its own correct copy.
The organism override also said 'Sphodromantis bioculata (praying mantis)'.
Root cause: this catalogue row was mistitled as a mantis paper when the assessments were written; the title was later corrected, but the assessment was not.
55.action_needed: Re-run the Consensus retrieval with questions about teratology, malformation as evidence for developmental rules, and Bateson's rule, then write the read-and-compare synthesis. Needs the Consensus API key. Until then the paper is catalogued and translated but carries no verdict.

17.summary: Same fault as id55: the stored assessment described a cabbage-white pupal-colour paper, not this stick-insect study. The dossier has been withdrawn rather than left wrong.
evidence: The stored verdict read 'Confirmed — pupal colour plasticity' and duplicated id14's record, which is the genuine Pieris pupa paper.
Dixippus morosus is hemimetabolous and has no pupal stage; the study scores adult females after the imaginal moult.
Root cause: this row was mistitled as a Pieris paper when the assessments were written; the title was later corrected, the assessment was not.
17.action_needed: Re-run the Consensus retrieval for light-dependent colour polyphenism in adult stick insects and write the synthesis. Note that two of the paper's six summary points claim transmission of modifications across parthenogenetic generations — part of the institute's abandoned inheritance programme — so the eventual verdict should not be a flat 'Confirmed'.

_eye_series_numbering.summary: Resolved September 2026 from the printed title pages and Crossref page numbers. The series in Arch. mikr. Anat. Entw.-Mech. 99 runs I (Przibram, methods, id 24), II (id 25, pp. 15–42), III physiology (id 26, pp. 43–57), IV growth (id 27, pp. 60–63), V Kolmer histology (id 28, pp. 64–75), VI colour (id 29, pp. 76–81), VII Jellinek training (id 30, pp. 82–103); Finkler I–III are ids 31–33. Translations, PDFs and DOIs were re-paired so each id is one article: translations 126→26, 158→27, 151→28, 131→29, 168→31, 165→32 (131 and 158 had also been attached to each other's PDF).
evidence: id27's PDF is filed as 'Die-Replantation-von-Augen-II-Physiology.pdf' and the site title says '(II: physiology)', but the paper's own H2 reads 'III. The Physiology of Replanted Mammalian Eyes.'
That paper's bibliography cites a Part II ('Haltbarkeit und Funktionsprufung', Akadem. Anz. 7/8, 1921) as a separate, earlier item.
id26 is filed as '(III: growth)'. There are six papers in this cluster (ids 25-30), so renumbering one risks a collision.
_eye_series_numbering.action_needed: None. Translation file names still carry the old numbering (internal only).

139_Wiesner_1923_Lens-replantation.summary: The results and summary sections are largely unreadable (garbled output), and the operation tables contain wrong counts (the print gives 11 self-grafts in perch where the translation says 4, and 2 same-species grafts in the spadefoot toad where it says 11). The header gives the wrong receipt date (print: 13 October 1922) and says 'Amphibians' for 'Animals'.
139_Wiesner_1923_Lens-replantation.public_note: This translation is being redone: its results and summary sections are unreliable and some table counts are wrong. Until then, please rely on the German original for anything beyond the methods.

100_Kammerer_1913_Inherited-colour-chang.summary: Summary point 13 breaks off mid-sentence and runs into point 14; in the German, Kammerer adds that no intrauterine or intra-ovarian induction was ever found.

56_Weiss_1923_Transplanted-limbs-II.summary: The translation reverses the graft direction for operation 065 and garbles page 169.

172_Ehrenpreis_1924_Spleen-transplantati.summary: One test series is called a 'replantation' although it was a second spleen implanted beside the host's own.

_autophor.summary: 'autophor' (Przibram's self-holding, suture-free graft method) was rendered as 'autoplastic(ally)' in titles and text. Titles are corrected; the running text still needs checking wherever the German has 'autophor'.
_autophor.action_needed: Replace 'autoplastic' by 'autophoric (suture-free)' where the German has 'autophor' — not where it has 'autoplastisch'.

_chunk_notes.summary: Leftover page-range notes from translation by sections: Secerov 1909 (summary point 1 continuation quoted in a note), Morgulis 1912 (an opening partial sentence), Przibram 1925 rat-tail length (first rows of Table XIV may be missing), Brecher 1924 Dixippus (results table garbled in translation). Four other such notes were removed in September 2026 because the text they described follows them.
_chunk_notes.action_needed: Check each against the German and restore any missing text.

_sept2026_fixed.summary: Fixed during the September 2026 review: wrong header notes in the translations of Abolin 1925 (named drugs it never used), Brecher & Winkler 1925 (authors), Weiss 1925 nerve dependence ('skeleton'), Thomson 1922 ('Amphibians'), Janda 1912 (part number), Klintz 1914 ('Lizards'), Kammerer 1909 ('epidemic' experiments), Kammerer 1907 (communication and species), Kolmer and Jellinek 1923 (authors); two mistranslations in Przibram 1917 (mean of 10 daily readings; young rats track the outside temperature more closely than mature ones); promotional translator's notes ('landmark', 'foreshadows', 'rediscovery target') removed from 109 translations.
